Aeneas. The Trojan hero and son of the goddess Aphrodite, he escaped Troy's destruction carrying his elderly father Anchises on his shoulders and leading his young son Ascanius to safety. Protected by his divine mother throughout the ten-year war, Aeneas fought bravely alongside Hector and the other Trojan princes. After Troy's fall, he was destined by Zeus and Fate to establish a settlement in Italy that would eventually become Rome. The Aeneid follows his seven-year journey from Troy across the Mediterranean, struggling against divine and human obstacles at every turn. Central to his story is his relationship with Dido of Carthage, a romance he was forced to abandon in order to fulfill his duty to found Rome. Aeneas represents the theme of destiny and duty superseding personal desire, unlike his Trojan peer Paris who chose personal desire and brought ruin to his entire civilization.
